new_findings.issue: When BLUX System is unavailable, an operation that attached an artifact loses its receipt: Runtime calls emit_artifact() before emit(receipt) inside one try block (runtime/blux_runtime/executor.py:445-450). emit_artifact() raises SINK_UNAVAILABLE, so emit() never runs and the receipt is neither stored nor spooled, contrary to system_sink.py:107 ("the receipt that lists them still is"). Every model.generate call attaches a model-call.json artifact (runtime/blux_runtime/models/capability.py:135-147), so this hits model and provider-failure receipts.
evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-06: echo.test plus one attached artifact, BluxSystemSink with a missing executable gives sink_error {code: SINK_UNAVAILABLE, spooled: false} and no outbox file; the same outage without an artifact spools the receipt (1 outbox line). The result itself is kept and the CLI reports NOT_RECORDED

Fixed in blux cfd7470 (OV-52, 2026-11-07): the receipt is always attempted, artifacts are spooled with their bytes, sink_error.missing_artifacts names any artifact not stored; tests/runtime/test_receipt_durability.py and tests/integration/test_blux_system.py (real blux-system)

new_findings.issue: BluxSystemSink.flush() reads the whole outbox, re-sends, then replaces the file with os.replace and no lock (runtime/blux_runtime/system_sink.py:127-147). A receipt that another process spools (emit() → _spool(), system_sink.py:97-102) between the read and the replace is silently deleted. Constitution: no hidden data loss.
evidence: Reproduced 2026-11-06 with two sinks on one outbox and a simulated interleaving: after flush() the outbox holds only the old receipt and the concurrently spooled one is gone (flush stats sent 0, remaining 1, refused 0)

Fixed in blux cfd7470 (OV-52, 2026-11-07): spool and flush serialized with a lock file; flush works from <outbox>.flushing.jsonl; two-process and killed-flush tests in tests/runtime/test_receipt_durability.py

new_findings.issue: No shipped entry point calls BluxSystemSink.flush(): spooled receipts are never retried, so they stay outside BLUX System indefinitely (the CLI does report NOT_RECORDED, cli/blux_cli/direct.py:441). Also, _retryable() treats every SINK_* code as retryable (system_sink.py:94-95), so a store refusal without its own code (SINK_REFUSED) is spooled and retried forever instead of being set aside.
evidence: `grep -rn outbox` and `grep -rn flush` over blux/cli, blux/runtime and blux-system (2026-11-06): flush() is defined only in runtime/blux_runtime/system_sink.py:127 and called only by tests/runtime/test_receipt_sinks.py
Fixed in blux cfd7470 (OV-52, 2026-11-07): `blux receipts status|flush`; `blux doctor` warns while receipts wait; SINK_REFUSED is no longer retryable

new_findings.issue: `fs.write` could write `.git/hooks/*`, `.git/config` and `.blux/` inside the workspace without approval, i.e. plant code that runs later outside BLUX's approvals.
evidence: Reproduced at 56c9b76: fs.write .git/hooks/pre-commit and .git/config succeeded (2026-11-06)
Fixed in blux 4163637 (OV-50, 2026-11-07): `workspace_write_needs_approval`; tests/runtime/test_tool_hardening.py::test_file_writes_into_git_and_blux_directories_need_an_approval

new_findings.issue: `shell.exec` read a command's whole output into memory before cutting it to 64 KiB.
evidence: Reproduced at 56c9b76: 400 MB of output raised peak RSS by about 765 MB (2026-11-06)

Fixed in blux 4163637 (OV-50, 2026-11-07): streams drained on threads keeping 64 KiB each; same probe +1 MB; tests/runtime/test_tool_hardening.py::test_shell_output_is_capped_while_it_is_read (tracemalloc peak < 8 MiB for 32 MiB)

new_findings.issue: `shell.exec` ignored the caller's cancellation: a cancelled `sleep 6` ran to the end and was reported as succeeded.
evidence: Reproduced at 56c9b76: cancel at 0.5 s, call returned succeeded after 6.1 s (2026-11-06)

Fixed in blux 4163637 (OV-50, 2026-11-07): the process group is killed and the call fails with reason `cancelled` (0.5 s); tests/runtime/test_tool_hardening.py::test_shell_honours_cancellation_and_kills_the_command

new_findings.issue: `blux agent` with no model configured printed only `model call failed: EXECUTION_FAILED` and exited 1, where `blux ask` lists the routes, a hint and the receipt and exits 3.
evidence: Reproduced at 56c9b76 with an empty environment (2026-11-06)
Fixed in blux 4163637 (OV-50, 2026-11-07): same report and exit codes as `blux ask`; tests/cli/test_agent_cmd.py::test_agent_without_a_model_says_why_and_exits_as_ask_does

new_findings.issue: `make lint` fails at BLUX HEAD: ruff reports 13 errors and 2 unformatted files in `training/dataset-program/` (added in 8d989de). Runtime, CLI, SDK and tests are clean.
evidence: `ruff check .` exit 1 and `ruff format --check .` 2 files at 56c9b76, all in training/dataset-program (2026-11-06)
Fixed in blux 60ddc76 (OV-53, 2026-11-07): formatted and lint-clean (preflight syntax tree unchanged); `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` exit 0 for the whole repository

new_findings.issue: `shell.exec` is confined only by its working directory, an allow-list environment and pattern-based command detection. It is not an OS sandbox: an approved or undetected command can read or write anywhere the user can, and a process that leaves the command's process group survives the call.
evidence: Recorded in the OV-50 report and ADR-0013 (2026-11-07); F89 narrowed the gap, it did not close it
new_findings.next_action: Adversarial drills in OV-62; decide whether shell.exec needs an OS-level sandbox before any release that enables it by default

new_findings.issue: A `scaffold` or `migrate` killed part-way left the repository between two plans with its journal `pending` and no way back: `lrc rollback` answered NOTHING_TO_ROLL_BACK, migrating back reported conflicts, later commands ran over the half-applied tree (with --force overwriting files whose only backup was in the abandoned journal), and two LRC processes could change one repository at once.
evidence: Reproduced at 443e532: migrate killed at its second file write; rollback exit 3 NOTHING_TO_ROLL_BACK, migrate back to v1 exit 1 MIGRATION_CONFLICT (2026-11-07)
Fixed in lrc ea82afc (OV-51, 2026-11-07): `lrc recover`, INTERRUPTED_TRANSACTION guard, fsynced backups, advisory lock (TARGET_LOCKED); tests/test_interrupted.py (5 tests, all fail on 443e532)
new_findings.next_action: Recovery is a CLI command, not a BLUX capability: through BLUX the INTERRUPTED_TRANSACTION error names it. Add a repo.recover capability only as a versioned contract change (OV-61)

new_findings.issue: A process killed after a change was recorded in the ledger, but before its journal was removed, made `ca recover` undo the recorded change: the ledger then said the changeset was both `applied` and `interrupted`, and `ca rollback` reported a false CONFLICT. A rollback killed before linking the undone entry left the same kind of contradiction.
evidence: Reproduced at 7cb953a: killed at the journal removal; recover reverted a.py, ledger [applied, interrupted], rollback CONFLICT (2026-11-07)

Fixed in blux-ca 689ec70 (OV-51, 2026-11-07): recover keeps a recorded change (`completed: true`) and repairs rollback links; tests/construction/test_interrupted_commit.py (2 tests, both fail on 7cb953a)

new_findings.issue: The SDK's `.blux/` loader (used by GOD and the BLUX runtime for every project under a root) followed symbolic links out of `.blux/`, blocked for ever on a named pipe, read a file whole before its 1 MiB check, and raised RecursionError on deeply nested YAML, so one hostile project could hang or crash discovery.
evidence: Reproduced at 4163637 through `god check`: pipe hung (timeout), link to /etc/passwd parsed, 100,000 `[` RecursionError traceback (2026-11-07)
Fixed in blux 9cd53ef (OV-51, 2026-11-07): regular files only (O_NOFOLLOW, non-blocking, fstat), bounded reads, nesting_too_deep; tests/sdk/test_dot_blux_hostile.py

new_findings.issue: YAML aliases were expanded without a bound: about 350 bytes took 24 s to check and each further level costs nine times more, in any `.blux/` file or YAML request read through the SDK.
evidence: Measured at 4163637: 258 bytes 0.3 s, 304 bytes 2.7 s, 350 bytes 24 s (2026-11-07)
Fixed in blux 9cd53ef (OV-51, 2026-11-07): expansion bounded by the byte limit (too_large), iterative check; 442 bytes refused in 0.7 s; no alias-free document within the limit is affected

new_findings.issue: GOD stopped on malformed input instead of reporting it: a hostile `.blux/` (pipe, link, deep nesting) hung or crashed the whole scan, and a damaged entry in the index cache crashed every later query (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError).
evidence: Reproduced at ad6f0c4 with a probe of 13 malformed projects and 7 damaged caches (2026-11-07)

Fixed in god 613b800 (OV-51, 2026-11-07): `.blux/` entries that are not regular files or directories are problems before anything is opened (also with older SDKs); cache entries carry a record digest and are re-read when damaged; tests/test_hostile_input.py (8 tests, all fail on ad6f0c4)
No false positives: `god check` over the 26 workspace repositories (secret-project excluded) is identical before and after (8 projects, 0 problems)

new_findings.issue: `coga replay` of a damaged artifact (engine not an object) crashed with AttributeError and exit 1, the "replay mismatch" code; a non-object linkage was reported as INTERNAL_ERROR, blaming CogA.
evidence: Reproduced at 3dc86fa (2026-11-07)
Fixed in blux-coga c94dc9c (OV-51, 2026-11-07): INVALID_ARTIFACT (exit 3); tests/reason/test_contract.py::test_replay_of_a_damaged_artifact_is_invalid_not_a_crash (4 cases)

new_findings.issue: A policy file nested too deeply to parse stopped DAT with INTERNAL_ERROR: RecursionError instead of INVALID_POLICY (it still failed closed, exit 3).
evidence: Reproduced at 487e1d4 (2026-11-07)
Fixed in dat 57c8099 (OV-51, 2026-11-07): INVALID_POLICY; tests/test_engine_policy.py::test_a_policy_nested_too_deeply_is_invalid_not_an_internal_error

new_findings.issue: A `create` killed while staging leaves its `.lrc-stage-*` directory beside the target. The target is never created and a later create succeeds, but nothing removes the stale directory.
evidence: Reproduced at ea82afc: killed at the second staged file (2026-11-07)
new_findings.next_action: Decide in OV-62 whether `create` may remove stale stage directories it can prove are its own

new_findings.issue: A crash between a record and its newline bricked the store: the record verified, the next append was written onto the same line, and from then on every open was STORE_CORRUPT, so every later receipt was refused.
evidence: Reproduced at f7f8ede: last newline removed, one ingest stored, reopen STORE_CORRUPT (2026-11-07)

Fixed in blux-system 26f2240 (OV-52, 2026-11-07): the newline is added and recorded (unterminated_record); a long-lived writer also repairs a torn tail left by another process; tests/test_evidence_authority.py

new_findings.issue: A shortened log verified as ok: whole records cut from the end, or an older copy of the log, left a valid chain. docs/STORE.md also claimed a re-hashed forgery was detected, which a hash chain alone cannot do.
evidence: Reproduced at f7f8ede: 2 of 3 records removed, verify ok:true (2026-11-07)

Fixed in blux-system 26f2240 (OV-52, 2026-11-07): head.json anchors the last record (truncated, anchor_mismatch); verify --expect-head checks a head kept elsewhere; STORE.md says what the chain proves; tests/test_evidence_authority.py
new_findings.next_action: The chain is unsigned: detecting a deliberate consistent rewrite needs an external head (see F113)

new_findings.issue: Corruption crashed readers instead of being reported: a record with recomputed hashes and a malformed payload raised KeyError on every command, an unknown receipt status crashed `graph`, and a damaged retention.json or a non-object store.json raised tracebacks. A newer store format was reported as corrupt without saying why.
evidence: Reproduced at f7f8ede with the OV-52 store probe (2026-11-07)

Fixed in blux-system 26f2240 (OV-52, 2026-11-07): STORE_CORRUPT with invalid_payload or details.reason (unsupported_version for a newer format); verify also checks payloads against Contract v1; tests/test_evidence_authority.py
False-positive guard: a receipt rejected before its capability was known (null capability_id) stays valid (caught by the BLUX integration suite during the stage, then covered by a test)

new_findings.issue: Retention could remove records without a record of it: the compacted log was installed first and the retention record appended afterwards, so a run killed in between left an unrecorded removal.
evidence: Reproduced at f7f8ede: retention killed before its record, log [] and verify ok:true (2026-11-07)

Fixed in blux-system 26f2240 (OV-52, 2026-11-07): the retention record (with previous_head and previous_records) is inside the new chain, installed with one rename; kills before and after the rename both leave a recorded state; tests/test_evidence_authority.py

new_findings.issue: Import could stop part-way and accepted malformed events: a conflict in the middle of a bundle left the first part imported, an event without a type crashed the import, and an event with an invalid operation id was stored. docs/STORE.md claimed nothing was written before the bundle was verified.
evidence: Reproduced at f7f8ede (2026-11-07)
Fixed in blux-system 26f2240 (OV-52, 2026-11-07): payloads and conflicts are checked before any write; a failing import imports nothing (imported_before_failure); tests/test_evidence_authority.py

new_findings.issue: Tampered or missing artifact blobs verified as ok (only artifact-verify per artifact noticed), re-ingesting the artifact with its bytes did not repair a damaged blob, and blobs were written outside the writer lock, where a retention run could prune one before its record existed.
evidence: Reproduced at f7f8ede (2026-11-07)
Fixed in blux-system 26f2240 (OV-52, 2026-11-07): verify reports blob_mismatch and blob_missing; re-ingest repairs; blob writes are fsynced and under the lock; tests/test_evidence_authority.py

new_findings.issue: Simultaneous writers were refused: the writer lock was non-blocking, so 15 of 16 simultaneous ingests got STORE_LOCKED, and BLUX spooled those receipts into an outbox nothing flushed (F85).
evidence: Measured at f7f8ede: 16 simultaneous writers, 1 stored and 15 STORE_LOCKED (2026-11-07)
Fixed in blux-system 26f2240 (OV-52, 2026-11-07): writers wait up to 10 s for the lock; 16 of 16 stored; tests/test_evidence_authority.py

new_findings.issue: A receipt BLUX System refused at emit time (invalid, conflict, corrupt store) was dropped: it was neither spooled nor set aside, although flush() already kept refused receipts in a refused file.
evidence: Source review of runtime/blux_runtime/system_sink.py at 9cd53ef (2026-11-07)

Fixed in blux cfd7470 (OV-52, 2026-11-07): refused documents are set aside in <outbox>.refused.jsonl (owner-only) and can be re-sent with `blux receipts flush --include-refused`; tests/runtime/test_receipt_durability.py

new_findings.issue: `blux agent` kept acting after a step's receipt was refused or lost: it recorded the operation as unrecorded and went on to run the tool calls it was asked for, so later actions had no receipt either.
evidence: Shown at 9cd53ef by tests/cli/test_agent_cmd.py, which expected the answer after a failing sink (2026-11-07)
Fixed in blux cfd7470 (OV-52, 2026-11-07): the agent stops before its next step when a receipt is neither recorded nor queued (ReceiptNotRecorded, exit 5); queued receipts still let it finish

new_findings.issue: The store's chain and head.json are unsigned, so someone who can write the store directory can rewrite both consistently; only a head kept elsewhere (verify --expect-head) detects that.
evidence: Documented in blux-system docs/STORE.md (OV-52, 2026-11-07)
new_findings.next_action: Decide in OV-63 (signing and release machinery) whether to sign or externally publish store heads, with a new key; the exposed key is never used

new_findings.issue: A one-shot command (`blux run`, `exec`, `ask`) still performs its action before it learns that BLUX System refuses the receipt; it then exits non-zero and the receipt is set aside. Only the agent loop can stop before a further action.
evidence: Design review (OV-52, 2026-11-07)
new_findings.next_action: Decide in OV-61 whether high-risk capabilities need a store health check before execution

new_findings.issue: The training pipeline's hidden-reasoning gate accepted reasoning-model output: `<think>` blocks (the format of Qwen3, the shortlisted base, and DeepSeek-R1), harmony analysis channels, and fields named `reasoning`, `reasoning_details`, `reasoning_summary`, `thought_process` or `thinking_blocks`. Provider chain-of-thought could have become training data.
evidence: Reproduced at cfd7470 with a gate probe: 6 of 9 reasoning forms accepted (2026-11-07)
Fixed in blux 60ddc76 (OV-53, 2026-11-07): markers and keys rejected; reasoning_structure and CogA reflection kept; tests/training/test_ov53_gates.py; pipeline 1.1.0
No false positives on the 127 train/validation records of blux-coga-dataset and blux-ca-dataset (aggregate counts)

new_findings.issue: The personal-data gate missed common forms: look-alike e-mail domains (`notexample.com` matched the `example.com` allowance), phone numbers without a country code or in international groups, IPv6, `/root` and Windows home paths, card numbers and US SSNs.
evidence: Reproduced at cfd7470: 11 of 14 probed forms passed unredacted (2026-11-07)

Fixed in blux 60ddc76 (OV-53, 2026-11-07): redacted (Luhn-checked cards, IPv6 with at least three groups so slices are kept); tests/training/test_ov53_gates.py including false-positive guards (slices, times, MACs, hashes, ids, documentation addresses)
new_findings.next_action: Bare 10-digit runs are deliberately not treated as phone numbers (ids look the same); private terms cover the rest

new_findings.issue: Reworded siblings of protected evaluation items could enter training: in one build, a lightly reworded copy of a holdout item was hash-assigned to train; in the next version, built with the previous split lock, siblings of the earlier holdout were accepted because the lock carries ids, not content, unless --protected was given.
evidence: Reproduced at cfd7470: 10 of 10 siblings of a v1 holdout item accepted into train/validation in v2 (2026-11-07)

Fixed in blux 60ddc76 (OV-53, 2026-11-07): siblings of a protected record in the same build are rejected; the previous dataset's protected splits are protected automatically from --lock; tests/training/test_ov53_gates.py

new_findings.issue: bluxgpt drops structured provider reasoning (DeepSeek reasoning_content, Anthropic thinking blocks) but passes inline `<think>` text from an OpenAI-compatible server through as answer text, so a local reasoning model (e.g. Qwen3 served without a reasoning parser) would put its chain-of-thought into answers and BLUX sessions.
evidence: Reproduced at 0175196 with the repository's fake provider: content '<think>PRIVATE INLINE</think>42' returned as output text unchanged (temporary probe test, not committed; 2026-11-07)
Training data is protected regardless: the blux_training gate now rejects `<think>` (F115)
new_findings.next_action: Strip leading reasoning blocks in openai_compat (also in streaming) with fake-provider tests; needs authorization (provider layer, OV-64 scope)

new_findings.issue: Four router dataset-integrity tests hard-coded the cloud /workspace layout and were always skipped elsewhere.
evidence: Fixed in blux 60ddc76 (OV-53, 2026-11-07): BLUX_COGA_DATASET and BLUX_COGA_DATASET_PYTHON select a checkout and its pinned environment; all 50 router tests pass here, with a positive control (the unmutated dataset passes the same probe)
